clue.text: Hint about returning TV panel show's set

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word is placed around the other

parts.note: a hint is a clue

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the show's name is read backwards

parts.note: QI is the BBC quiz and panel show hosted first by Stephen Fry

explanation.surface: A hint about the set of a TV panel show coming back for a new series.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is an exclusive circle of people, and set is a common synonym for such a social group.

clue.text: Bread releasing a single recorded as DIY music?

indicators.note: releasing means letting go, so the named letter is dropped from the bread

parts.note: a loaf of bread
the letter released from the bread
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A home baker letting a single go out, recorded in a do-it-yourself way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a single' reads as a record release, but the A is what the bread lets go and single is the numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lo-fi music is recorded cheaply at home with basic equipment, a hallmark of the do-it-yourself scene.

clue.text: Mike casting actress in The Krays, say

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: casting a part rearranges who plays whom, so these letters are dealt out afresh

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named Mike chooses an actress for a film about the Kray twins.
explanation.walkthrough: The Krays were notorious East London gangster twins of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangsters such as the Kray twins are criminals, examples of wrongdoers or villains.

clue.text: Mister Scrooge partook occasionally at first

indicators.note: at first says the kept letters come before the miser in the build
occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
Dickens's Scrooge is the archetypal miser

explanation.surface: Mr Scrooge sometimes shared in things at the start of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister' looks like a title for Scrooge, but read it as one who mists: a spray device.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser turns liquid into a fine spray, so it is literally something that mists.

clue.text: Colour once the line's blue

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
L is an abbreviation for line
feeling blue is feeling low

explanation.surface: A colour that used to mark a line is now blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' signals an old form: YE is how 'the' was written in olden times, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is a primary colour of the spectrum, the shade of lemons and egg yolks.

clue.text: Belly dance finally seen by Arab country's royal bodyguard

indicators.note: seen by means placed next to, so the country simply follows
finally points at the end of each word, so only its closing letter counts

parts.note: the last letters of the two words
the sultanate on the Arabian Peninsula

explanation.surface: A belly dance performed in Oman, watched by a king's guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yeomen of the Guard are the British monarch's ceremonial bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeoman, as in Yeoman of the Guard, is a member of the sovereign's ceremonial protective corps.

clue.text: Grown-up weed over tent

parts.note: a grown-up is big

indicators.note: over suggests turning something over, so the drug word is read backwards

parts.note: weed and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: An adult smoking cannabis in a tent, as at a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: The big top is the large main tent of a circus.

clue.text: Brave to pick unknown

parts.note: to pick a flower is to pluck it
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: It takes courage to choose something you know nothing about.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucky means having pluck, courage in the face of difficulty.

clue.text: See 14
Son left boring low buzzer — it's annoying

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the first pair of pieces goes inside the other word

parts.note: a cow lows, that is moos
S is the abbreviation for son
to quit a job is to have left it

explanation.surface: A son walked out of something dull, which is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective for the buzzer but is the verb a cow does.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosquito is the whining insect whose buzzing at night is notoriously irritating.

clue.text: Affected American grounds for education

parts.note: camp means exaggerated, theatrical or affected
the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A pretentious American gives reasons for wanting schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds' reads as reasons, but here it means land, as in school grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the land and buildings of a university or college.

clue.text: Leader of air force travelling to this address

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters change places
the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter
the rest of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An air force commander is posted to this location.
explanation.definitionFit: Care of, written c/o, directs post to someone at another person's address.

clue.text: Material lie about modern American composer

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
re means concerning or about
Philip Glass, the American minimalist composer

explanation.surface: A substantial untruth told about a contemporary US composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' reads as an adjective (important), but it is the noun: a substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibreglass is a material made from fine glass fibres, used in boats and insulation.

clue.text: Getting souvenir from Gatwick's terminal: go back with Japanese drink

indicators.note: terminal means at the end, so only the last letter of the airport is kept

parts.note: the final letter

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the other direction, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for to urinate
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Buying a memento at a Gatwick terminal before heading back with some sake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal' looks like the airport building, but it means the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small item kept in memory of a person or place, much like a souvenir.

clue.text: Duke only bet big on poker when working with electronic system for recording deals

indicators.note: working means being put through processes, so these letters are reorganised

parts.words: Duke only bet big on poker
parts.note: the main body of letters to be rearranged
E is the abbreviation for electronic

explanation.surface: An aristocrat gambles heavily on poker played on an electronic machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-entry bookkeeping records every transaction twice, as debit and credit, so it is an accounting method.

clue.text: Conservative party pursuing alternative to holding hard vote

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the party piece follows what precedes it

parts.note: or offers an alternative

indicators.note: holding means having inside, so the letter for hard sits within the short word before it

parts.note: taken as written
H is the pencil grade for hard
a do is a party
a cross on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A Conservative party trailing an alternative while trying to secure a firm vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' looks like the political party, but it means traditional in outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodox means adhering to established beliefs and practices, so traditional or conservative.

clue.text: Pressure of rubber company making ten hollow samples

indicators.note: making here means turning into, so one letter becomes something else
hollow means emptied out, leaving just the outside letters of the word that follows

parts.note: Durex is a condom brand
X is the Roman numeral for ten
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A condom maker under pressure to produce ten empty samples.
explanation.walkthrough: Durex is a well-known condom brand; its final X, the ten, is turned into SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is coercion or pressure, as in a confession made under duress.

clue.text: Iconic Australian posh girl raised pulse

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the emu is Australia's national bird, on its coat of arms
gel is how a posh speaker says girl

explanation.surface: A famous Australian raising a well-off young woman's heart rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' suggests a heartbeat, but it is the food: peas, beans and lentils.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is an edible seed such as a lentil or chickpea, and legume is the botanical term for such a plant.

clue.text: Quickly prepare comic set with RuPaul trashing America

indicators.note: comic means funny or absurd, so the letters are rearranged playfully
trashing means throwing away, so the country's letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: Quickly putting together a comedy set with the drag star RuPaul, while slating America.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle up a meal is to make it quickly from whatever is to hand.

clue.text: Retrospectively consider casting couches untouchable

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking backwards, so the letters are read from right to left
couches can mean holds within, so the letters lie inside the words before it

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Looking back on the casting couch, which should have been off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casting couches' suggests the film-industry scandal, but couches is the verb: it holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacred is holy and so beyond criticism or interference: it must not be touched.

clue.text: My class stays

parts.note: cor, like my, is an exclamation of surprise
a set is a teaching class grouped by ability

explanation.surface: My class remains where it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stays' reads as a verb but is the noun: the stiffening strips of a corset, and the garment itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays was the old name for a corset, from the boned strips that stiffened it.

clue.text: Shy away from angry crocodile wanting fish

indicators.note: something angry is worked up and disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order
wanting means lacking, so the fish's letters are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
the cod is a common fish

explanation.surface: Backing away from a furious crocodile that is hungry for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to flinch or draw back in fear or disgust.

clue.text: A lot of our menus circulated

indicators.note: circulated means sent round, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Many copies of the restaurant's menus were handed round.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerous means great in number, many, so it substitutes for a lot of before a plural noun.

clue.text: Club's highest point when midfielder initially moves up top

indicators.note: moving up to the top in a down clue means this letter now begins the word
initially means at the start, so just the opening letter of the player is used

parts.note: the first letter
the acme is the peak or summit

explanation.surface: A football club's finest moment comes when its midfielder pushes forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The M of ACME is lifted from third place to the front, turning ACME into MACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy club with a spiked or flanged head, a medieval weapon.

clue.text: Partner's steep parking charges

indicators.note: charges can mean is entrusted with, holding something in its care, so one word takes in the letter

parts.note: to souse is to soak or steep
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: My other half complains about expensive car park fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like an adjective for high prices, but it is the verb to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse is a husband or wife, one's partner in marriage.

clue.text: Space on school English programme

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the space follows the school piece

parts.note: SCH is an abbreviation for school
an em is a printer's space
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Room on the school's English syllabus.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a plan or systematic programme of action.
